candidate.analysis: Analyze /input/public_csv, filtering debates whose philosophical or debate topic contains “ethic”. Report sample size, outcome summary, Pearson correlations between percentage increase in utilitarian advocacy and numeric predictors, and grouped outcome means by moderator ethical stance and critical-event occurrence. Missing or nonnumeric values are omitted per calculation. This describes associations only and does not establish causality.
candidate.answer: Among 259 ethics-focused debates, the percentage increase in utilitarian advocacy averaged 17.330% (range 0–100). Its correlation with audience interest was negligible (r=-0.006), while correlations with average debate duration (r=0.074) and number of sessions (r=0.053) were very weakly positive; argument intensity had no estimable Pearson correlation (r=NA; paired_n=259). Utilitarian moderators were associated with a much higher mean increase (65.189%, n=68) than deontological (0.054%, n=103) or virtue-ethics moderators (0.570%, n=88). Debates with critical events had a higher mean increase (29.441%, n=107) than those without (6.143%, n=118); missing-event rows averaged 18.046% (n=34). These are descriptive associations and do not establish causality.
